rule_or_note: Full enriched population (10,000 rows) used as the audit denominator.
Parsed signup dates retained for cohort analysis; span 2020-08-06 to 2026-01-26 across 66 calendar months. Inverted pairs are retained here because signup_date is individually valid.
Blank/'not_a_date' rows coerced to NaT in E3; excluded from all signup series.
Parsed last-purchase dates retained for activity analysis; span 2020-08-06 to 2026-01-25 across 66 calendar months. Inverted pairs are retained here because last_purchase_date is individually valid.
Blank/'missing' rows coerced to NaT in E3; excluded from all activity series.
Rows with both dates present (KPI-5 denominator).

last_purchase_date < signup_date (KPI-5 anomaly): conditioned to NaN in customer_tenure_days and excluded from KPI-5, but retained in standalone signup and last-purchase series to avoid selection bias (see signup_rows_if_inverted_excluded).
last_purchase_date >= signup_date (KPI-5 numerator); source of valid tenure.
Non-negative (last_purchase_date - signup_date) durations in days; identical to the chronologically valid dual-date count by construction.
Inverted pairs conditioned to NaN rather than sign-flipped.
Rows missing at least one date; tenure left as NaN with no imputation.

Counterfactual audit (rejected): dropping inverted pairs from the single-date signup series would discard 829 late signups and bias monthly signup volume downward (quantified as a rejected sensitivity row in m6_trend_tests.csv), so inverted pairs stay in the signup series.

Counterfactual audit (rejected): dropping inverted pairs from the single-date activity series would discard 829 early last purchases and bias monthly activity upward (quantified as a rejected sensitivity row in m6_trend_tests.csv), so inverted pairs stay in the activity series.

Temporal series are built from single-date fields: NaT signup/last-purchase dates (from 'not_a_date'/'missing' sentinels and blanks) are excluded, while the 829 is_date_inverted rows are retained because each individual date is valid. Inverted pairs are excluded only from dual-date metrics (customer_tenure_days, KPI-5); dropping them from single-date series would systematically discard late signups and early last purchases and fabricate a spurious trend. Pairwise/cohort n is always reported.
